#192 implement.summary: Committed 0eca8679 on fix/192-ci-runs-python-3-13 in /tmp/wt-192. It has not been pushed, and main is still 8f7d98aa. (1) The ci.yml test matrix is now 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 on both ubuntu-latest and windows-latest: six lint+test legs instead of four. A new test, tests/test_ci_python_matrix.py, works out the minor versions from install.sh's AELIX_PYTHON default and checks the matrix equals them. It also checks both runners with no include/exclude, fail-fast off, a separate check name per leg, the floor equal to every pyproject's requires-python floor, and .python-version being one of the legs. Its regex tolerates CRLF line endings. (2) The whole suite under 3.13 at 8f7d98aa failed 11 tests, all from one product defect that ADR-0241 had already named. _strict_hint was a denylist: on a strict interpreter, any verify code outside 2/18/19/20 was told 'RFC 5280 rule, not trust; reinstall on 3.12'. That included a bad signature (7), a non-CA issuer (79) and every error with no code. It is now an allowlist of codes 78 and 80-94: OpenSSL's strict-mode block minus 79, which I measured being raised without the strict flag. An error with no code is matched by OpenSSL's message text for those codes. Real handshakes show 'Missing Authority Key Identifier' is code 85, not the 95 the repo used (95 is RPK_UNTRUSTED). I corrected it in the code, the TLS guide and its bundled copy, and the tests. In test_tls_strict, the two rows that asserted a pre-3.13 interpreter now force 3.12's flags instead. New rows cover both sides of the allowlist, plus three real handshakes measured with strict on and off. (3) release.yml stays on 3.12, with the reason in a comment: it runs no tests, and wheels built under 3.12 and 3.13 are byte-identical. (4) No timeout-minutes is set, concurrency is per-ref, and no test or doc pins a job count. Branch protection still requires only the four 3.11/3.12 checks by name. (5) Windows 3.13's finer monotonic clock: I read the timing-sensitive tests and found no tie assumption that a finer clock would break. That is a reading only; the branch CI's windows py3.13 leg is what proves it. Docs updated: ADR-0241 dated amendment and index row, installer comments, getting-started and the TLS guide plus bundled copies, README, README.ko, CONTRIBUTING, 05-post-beta-direction, CHANGELOG.

blocking.title: Strict mode can raise code 79 on its own, but HEAD now sends every 79 to the CA advice, and the docs say strict never causes it
blocking.detail: The allowlist drops 79 because a CA:FALSE intermediate fails with 79 whether strict is on or off. That is only one way to get 79. OpenSSL also raises 79 for a trust anchor whose X509_check_ca result is not 1, and in that case only under strict. Measured: a root with no basicConstraints but with keyUsage keyCertSign (an old appliance shape) fails with 79 when strict is on and passes when it is off, on both the 3.12 and 3.13 interpreters (OpenSSL 3.5.6). On 3.13, any path that does not measure the failure now gets the CA advice for that root. Base gave the strict advice there, which was correct, so this commit regresses that case. Every Google adapter call takes this path, and so does any error whose host cannot be recovered. Text this makes false: the TLS guide and its bundled copy say 'The whole strict-only set is codes 78 and 80-94' and that 79 'gets the advice for that failure even with strict on, because strict did not cause it'. The CHANGELOG says 'Only the codes OpenSSL raises solely under strict mode (78 and 80-94)'. The ADR-0241 amendment and the _error_hints comment imply 79 is not strict's to claim. The test_tls_strict message for _NOT_STRICT_ONLY[79] says 'strict claimed a failure it cannot cause'. The code alone cannot tell the two 79 cases apart, so 79 needs a hedged remedy (for example the strict remedy's openssl s_client confirm step plus the CA option), and the docs need correcting.
blocking.evidence: Kit: .omc/probes/192-live/verify/KIT.txt (B1). handshakes-head.txt has the row 'root_no_bc_ku_kcs strict-on: code=79 ... strict-off: ok' on 3.12.13 and on 3.13.13. Real CLI, Google adapter, certifi path (truststore stubbed to fail), SSL_CERT_FILE set to that root, outputs in cli-outputs/. cli-g-head312-79.txt: TLS succeeds and the server's 500 comes back. cli-g-head313-79.txt (HEAD): 'invalid CA certificate' followed by 'point SSL_CERT_FILE at a bundle that includes it', although SSL_CERT_FILE already is that bundle. cli-g-base313-79.txt (8f7d98aa): the strict remedy. The openrouter CLI against the same server (cli-head313-nobcroot79.txt) relaxed strict by aelix's own measurement and reached the server, so aelix itself treats this 79 as strict-only.

blocking.title: The failure counts and their classification in the ADR, CHANGELOG, commit message and test docstrings are wrong
blocking.detail: At 8f7d98aa under 3.13.13 there are 11 failures, but they are not 'every one a TLS remedy' or 'all this one defect'. Nine are the remedy defect: test_error_hints x6, test_provider_error_quoting_186, test_terminal_text and test_login_wizard. The other two are guard asserts that assumed a pre-3.13 interpreter. test_tls_strict::test_nothing_happens_when_strict_is_already_off and ::test_the_advice_stops_naming_a_ca_the_user_already_installed both fail on 'assert strict_is_enabled() is False'. Text that is false as a result: the ADR-0241 amendment ('every one a TLS remedy', 'they were a product defect, as it said'), the ADR index row ('11건 ... 전부 제품 결함'), the CHANGELOG ('all this one defect') and the commit message ('every one the strict remedy on a non-strict failure'). The test texts say 'ten' (tests/test_ci_python_matrix.py docstring: 'ten tests that only a 3.13 run could see'; test_tls_strict.py comment: 'The 3.13 suite failed ten rows on exactly that'), but the real numbers are 9 plus 2. This needs a text fix only.
blocking.evidence: base313-subset.txt holds 8f7d98aa's tests and product under venv313, run over tests/providers tests/tui tests/oauth tests/agents tests/cli tests/status: '11 failed, 6544 passed, 21 skipped'. The two test_tls_strict FAILED lines show the guard 'assert strict_is_enabled() is False' (base source read with git show 8f7d98aa:tests/providers/test_tls_strict.py). The other nine assert 'SSL_CERT_FILE' in a strict-remedy string.

nonblocking.title: Pre-existing, outside #192: on macOS and Windows with truststore, a TLS failure gets no remedy
nonblocking.detail: When truststore verifies through the OS, the message ('certificate is not trusted') carries no _TLS_MARKERS text, and httpcore's 'from None' hides the SSLCertVerificationError from attribution. The CLI therefore prints the bare error with no hint. This commit does not change that. For OS verifier codes (negative CFError values, HRESULT values) it now gives the CA advice where base gave the strict advice, which is better.
